<parameter=text>GO — but with a major concentration-risk caveat.

**Your current GME position:**
• 85 shares at an average cost of $42.12/share
• Current price: ~$19.89 (already down ~53% from your cost basis)

**Cost to double the position (85 more shares at your $42.12 avg cost):**
• 85 × $42.12 = **$3,580.20**

**Your available liquidity:**
• Checking: $47,488.06
• Savings: $16,413.28
• Credit-card headroom: $1,649.00
• **Total: ~$65,550.34**

**Affordability verdict: Yes, you can easily afford it.** The $3,580.20 is only about 5.5% of your combined liquid resources. Even using checking alone, you'd still have ~$43,900 left.

**Concentration-risk caveat:** GME is already underwater by roughly 53%. Doubling down at your original average cost would mean committing ~$7,160 total to a single, highly volatile meme stock. While it would lower your effective average cost if the stock recovers, it also doubles your dollar exposure to further downside. If GME dropped another 50%, you'd be looking at ~$3,580 in additional losses on top of what you've already lost. This is a classic "catching a falling knife" scenario — financially feasible, but from a portfolio-diversification standpoint, concentrating more capital in a single speculative name is risky.</parameter>
